_note: Walmart facts database. Add, edit or remove strings in the "facts" list. Please verify figures before publishing, since numbers change over time.
facts: Bananas are Walmart's top-selling grocery item, with well over a billion pounds sold each year.
Walmart is the largest private employer in the United States.
As of fiscal year 2025, Walmart employed about 2.1 million associates around the world.
As of fiscal year 2025, about 270 million customers and members shopped with Walmart each week.
As of fiscal year 2025, Walmart operated more than 10,750 stores and clubs in 19 countries.
Walmart's "Everyday Low Prices" promise is a core part of how the company has operated since Sam Walton's early days.
Walmart is headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas, just a short drive from where Sam Walton opened his first store.
Walmart runs one of the largest private truck fleets in the United States.
Sam Walton's "Ten Foot Rule": whenever you come within ten feet of a customer, look them in the eye, greet them and ask if you can help.
In 1987 Walmart completed one of the largest private satellite communications systems in the country, connecting its stores to headquarters.
Walmart opened its first Neighborhood Market in 1998 and launched online shopping on Walmart.com in 2000.
Sam Walton was born on March 29, 1918, in Kingfisher, Oklahoma.
Sam Walton married Helen Robson on February 14, 1943.
In 1945, Sam Walton bought a Ben Franklin variety store franchise in Newport, Arkansas.
Sam Walton opened Walton's 5&10 on the Bentonville, Arkansas, town square in 1950.
The first Walmart Discount City opened on July 2, 1962, in Rogers, Arkansas.
Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. was incorporated on October 31, 1969.
Walmart's stock was first offered to the public on October 1, 1970.
Walmart stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange in 1972.
Sam's Club opened its first location in 1983 in Midwest City, Oklahoma.
Walmart's first Supercenter opened in 1988 in Washington, Missouri.
Walmart's first international store opened in Mexico in 1991.
Walmart entered Canada in 1994 by acquiring 122 Woolco stores.
By 1995, Walmart had stores in all 50 U.S. states.
Walmart opened its first store in China, in Shenzhen, in 1996.
Walmart joined the Dow Jones Industrial Average in 1997.
Walmart entered the United Kingdom in 1999 by acquiring the Asda supermarket chain.
In 2002, Walmart ranked number one on the Fortune 500 for the first time.
President George H. W. Bush presented Sam Walton with the Presidential Medal of Freedom in March 1992.
Sam Walton's autobiography, Made in America, was published in 1992.
Walmart introduced its Spark symbol and dropped the hyphen from its name in 2008.
Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for about $3.3 billion.
Walmart bought about 77% of India's Flipkart in 2018 for roughly $16 billion.
Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. officially became Walmart Inc. in February 2018.
The Walmart Museum in Bentonville is housed in Sam Walton's original Walton's 5&10 building, and admission is free.
The Walmart Museum's Spark Cafe is a vintage-style soda fountain that serves Sam Walton's favorite flavor, butter pecan.
Sam Walton's 1979 Ford F-150 pickup truck is on display at the Walmart Museum.
Walmart's four core values are Service to the Customer, Respect for the Individual, Strive for Excellence and Act with Integrity.
The Walmart cheer spells out W-A-L-M-A-R-T and ends with "Who's number one? The customer! Always!"
Sam Walton's Sundown Rule: take care of customer requests by sundown instead of putting them off.
Sam Walton's Rule 1 for building a business: commit to your business and believe in it more than anybody else.
Sam Walton's Rule 2: share your profits with all your associates and treat them as partners.
Sam Walton's Rule 3: motivate your partners, because money and ownership alone aren't enough.
Sam Walton's Rule 4: communicate everything you possibly can to your partners.
Sam Walton's Rule 5: appreciate everything your associates do for the business.
Sam Walton's Rule 6: celebrate your success and find some humor in your failures.
Sam Walton's Rule 7: listen to everyone in your company, especially the people on the front lines.
Sam Walton's Rule 8: exceed your customers' expectations.
Sam Walton's Rule 9: control your expenses better than your competition.
Sam Walton's Rule 10: swim upstream and ignore conventional wisdom.
In fiscal year 2025, Walmart's total revenue was about $681 billion.
Walmart's global eCommerce sales topped $100 billion for the first time in fiscal year 2024.
Roughly 90% of Americans live within 10 miles of a Walmart store.
In 2021, Walmart pledged to buy an additional $350 billion of U.S.-made products by 2031.
Walmart aims for zero emissions in its own global operations by 2040, without using carbon offsets.
Walmart's Project Gigaton reached its goal of avoiding 1 billion metric tons of emissions six years early.
Walmart announced its RFID tag requirement for top suppliers in 2003.
Walmart InHome, which delivers groceries into customers' homes, launched in 2019.
Walmart+ launched in September 2020 with free delivery from stores, fuel savings and Scan & Go.
Walmart started its $4 generic prescription program on September 22, 2006, in the Tampa, Florida, area.
By late November 2006, Walmart's $4 generic prescription program was available at all of its U.S. pharmacies.
Great Value, Walmart's largest private brand, launched in 1993.
Walmart stores have been closed on Thanksgiving Day since 2020.
Walmart entered Germany in 1997 by buying the Wertkauf hypermarket chain, and left the German market in 2006.
Walmart bought the video streaming service Vudu in 2010 and sold it to Fandango in 2020.
Walmart took a 51% controlling stake in South Africa's Massmart in 2011.
Massmart, Walmart's South African subsidiary, operates brands including Game and Makro.
Walmart bought the menswear brand Bonobos in 2017 for $310 million.
In 2021, Walmart sold a majority stake in Asda to the Issa brothers and TDR Capital.
Walmart acquired Chile's Lider supermarket chain, part of D&S, in 2009.
Walmart de México is Walmart's largest international market and one of the largest private employers in Mexico.
In Mexico, Walmart operates under banners including Bodega Aurrera, Walmart Supercenter and Sam's Club.
Walmart Canada operates about 400 stores.
Walmart's India business includes Flipkart and Best Price wholesale stores.
Walmart named its Ol' Roy dog food after Sam Walton's favorite bird-hunting dog, an English setter.
In 1984, Sam Walton danced the hula on Wall Street after Walmart met his pre-tax profit goal of 8%.
Sam Walton flew his own small plane to scout store locations and drop in on stores.
Sam Walton insisted on calling Walmart's employees "associates" to reflect a partnership.
Walmart's yellow Smiley mascot debuted in 1990 and returned to Walmart advertising in 2016.
Sam's Choice, a Walmart private brand named for Sam Walton, launched in 1991.
A typical Walmart Supercenter is about 178,000 square feet.
Walmart Pay, which lets shoppers pay by scanning a QR code in the Walmart app, launched in 2015.
Walmart's Fight Hunger. Spark Change. campaign has supported Feeding America food banks since 2014.
For fiscal year 2025, Walmart's global giving, including in-kind donations, was approximately $2 billion.
Walmart's Live Better U education benefit launched in September 2018.
Since July 2021, Live Better U has covered 100% of tuition and books for eligible associates.
Eligible Walmart associates facing emergencies such as disasters can apply for hardship grants that don't need to be repaid.
Walmart U.S. net sales were about $462.4 billion in fiscal year 2025.
Sam's Club U.S. net sales were about $90.2 billion in fiscal year 2025.
Walmart International net sales were about $121.9 billion in fiscal year 2025.
As of January 31, 2025, Walmart U.S. had 3,559 Supercenters.
As of January 31, 2025, Walmart U.S. operated 4,605 retail units.
Walmart has raised its dividend every year for more than 50 years, earning "Dividend King" status.
Walmart completed a 3-for-1 stock split in February 2024.
In December 2025, Walmart moved its stock listing from the NYSE to Nasdaq and kept the WMT ticker.
Walmart's store-based delivery network reaches more than 90% of U.S. households with same-day delivery.
Walmart partners with Zipline and Wing to deliver orders by drone from store locations.
Walmart launched Express Delivery, with orders arriving in about two hours, in 2020.
Sam's Club introduced its Member's Mark private brand in 1998.
As of fiscal year 2025, Sam's Club operated about 600 clubs in the United States and Puerto Rico.
Sam's Club was named after Walmart founder Sam Walton.
Sam's Club Scan & Go lets members skip the checkout line by scanning items and paying with their phones.
About 75% of Walmart's U.S. salaried store, club and supply chain managers started as hourly associates.
Walmart has about 1.6 million associates in the United States.
Walmart's Associate Stock Purchase Plan offers a 15% company match on the first $1,800 contributed each year.
Walmart matches associate 401(k) contributions dollar for dollar up to 6% of eligible pay.
Walmart associates get a 10% discount on general merchandise, fresh fruit and vegetables and most regularly priced items.
Walmart launched Project Gigaton in 2017 to avoid 1 billion metric tons of supply chain emissions by 2030.
Walmart operates about 4,600 pharmacies in the United States.
Walmart is the largest grocery retailer in the United States.
Walmart holds roughly one-fifth of the U.S. grocery market.
Walmart's new Bentonville home office campus began opening in 2025 and is designed for more than 15,000 associates.
The Walton family owns roughly 45% of Walmart's shares.
Helen Walton, Sam Walton's wife, passed away on April 19, 2007, at age 87.
Sam Walton passed away on April 5, 1992, at age 74.
In 1980, Walmart had 276 stores and reached $1 billion in annual sales.
In 1970, Walmart operated 38 stores.
The first Walmart opened at the corner of Walnut Street and 8th Street in Rogers, Arkansas.
Sam Walton moved to Bentonville after his Newport landlord refused to renew the store's lease.
Walmart's bettergoods food brand launched in 2024.
Walmart's onn. consumer electronics brand launched in 2019.
Marketside, Walmart's fresh prepared food brand, got its start in 2008.
Walmart works with Symbotic to bring robotic automation to its regional distribution centers.
Walmart's Alphabot robotic system powers Market Fulfillment Centers that help pick online grocery orders.
Sparky is Walmart's AI shopping assistant in the Walmart app.
Walmart Global Tech has engineering hubs in Bentonville, Silicon Valley, Bengaluru and Chennai.
Walmart has set a goal of powering its operations with 100% renewable energy by 2035.
Walmart aims to protect, manage or restore 50 million acres of land and 1 million square miles of ocean by 2030.
Walmart plans to build its own EV fast-charging network at thousands of Walmart and Sam's Club locations by 2030.
Spark Driver is Walmart's app for independent contractors who deliver orders from its stores.
Walmart+ includes free delivery from store on orders over $35 and free shipping with no order minimum.
In 2013, Walmart pledged to hire 100,000 U.S. military veterans.
Spark Good Round Up lets customers round their Walmart.com or Walmart app purchases up to the nearest dollar to donate to charity.
Walmart offers same-day pharmacy delivery.
Sam Walton graduated from the University of Missouri in 1940 with a degree in economics.
Sam Walton became the youngest Eagle Scout in Missouri history at the time.
Sam Walton started his retail career at a J.C. Penney store in Des Moines, Iowa, in 1940.
Sam Walton served in the U.S. Army Intelligence Corps during World War II.
Sam Walton bought his Newport store with $5,000 of his own savings and a $20,000 loan from his father-in-law.
Walmart's three Basic Beliefs are Respect for the Individual, Service to our Customers and Strive for Excellence.
Sam Walton brought the Walmart cheer home after seeing factory workers do a company cheer on a 1975 trip to Korea.
Walmart's Saturday morning meetings in Bentonville were a company tradition where managers reviewed results and shared ideas.
Texas has more Walmart stores than any other state.
The first Walmart Neighborhood Market opened on October 7, 1998, in Bentonville, Arkansas.
Walmart introduced the tagline "Save money. Live better." in September 2007, replacing "Always Low Prices. Always."
From 1992 to 2008, Walmart's logo used a star in place of the hyphen in its name.
Walmart began piloting Pickup Towers in stores in late 2016.
A Walmart Neighborhood Market is about 40,000 square feet.
Walmart Supercenters combine general merchandise and a full grocery department under one roof.
Walmart Neighborhood Markets focus on groceries, with fresh produce, meat, bakery, deli and a pharmacy.
